# @guowenzhang/dsh-ui-beautify
English | 中文
## Background
A third-party interface enhancement plugin for DeepSeek Harness, focused on **mobile usability**: ma
king conversations, the sidebar, and settings easier to use on small screens.
It also offers independent body and code font choices, custom logos, icons, names and welcome taglin
es, and translation of English skill and plugin descriptions into the interface language using the d
efault model. Other improvements include recent conversation tabs, upward navigation through your se
nt questions (which loads the older page once the loaded history runs out), a floating one-line prev
iew of the round you are reading that jumps back to its start, a composer light beam, and desktop qu
ound you are reading that jumps back to its start, a composer light beam, and desktop quick replies.
Every choice on the settings page reports its own write: the row says it is saving, confirms when th
e value landed, and offers a retry when the Host refuses it. The name and tagline fields wait for an
input method to finish before they commit, so confirming a candidate never saves half a word.
On phones whose browser predates the newest JavaScript APIs, the plugin completes the ones the PDF e
ngine calls, so PDF and Word/PowerPoint previews open instead of failing with `... is not a function
ine calls, so PDF and Word/PowerPoint previews open instead of failing with `... is not a function`.
## Installation
Requires DeepSeek Harness **0.2.0-rc.1 or newer**. This example uses the `web` profile:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Restart the corresponding host and reload the browser, then open **Settings → UI Beautify**. Click *
*Translate descriptions** to generate translations; this uses the default model's quota, caches resu
lts, and leaves original files unchanged.
Translations sharing the same local data directory are deduplicated across host processes, including
recovery after an owner exits. Unknown locks are preserved rather than deleted. Recovery retains sm
all generation-marker directories to prevent stale processes from taking a newer lock; do not clean
these markers while any host is running.
## Version and upgrade
General settings gains one line under **Current version**: the newest release published to the deskt
op shell's own update feed, with an **Upgrade** button beside it. The button opens the shell's exist
ing update flow, so downloading and installing stay with the updater that owns them; when the runnin
g install is already the newest release, the line says so and the button is disabled.
The line appears only where a feed exists. A desktop build carries `resources/app-update.yml` naming
its feed URL and channel, which is what the row reads; a plain `dsh web` install has no such file a
nd sees no row. A deployment that publishes elsewhere — an internal mirror, a different channel — na
mes its manifest explicitly:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Recent conversations
Recent conversations have their own switch in **Settings → UI Beautify** and do not require the code
work view or mobile adaptation. The strip shows up to five eligible conversations in activity order
; selecting one does not reorder it. Tabs use the host theme tokens in light and dark mode, includin
g when the host has no conversation/trace tab bar.
On desktop the strip is a hemp line pinned to the header's left and right edges. Up to five recent c
onversations hang from it on clothespins in the middle, the selected conversation is tinted, and the
line sags toward the middle. The line shares the row with the host conversation/trace tabs, which s
tay clickable; the header grows by the line height. When the header narrows, the tags shrink and the
n move to their own row below the host tabs, and the line still reaches both edges. At widths of 600
px or less, phones keep the previous text-tab strip and hide the host view tabs. A host-native recen
t strip takes precedence. Disabling recent conversations or unloading the plugin removes the strip a
nd restores the host tabs.
For development, `pnpm run test:recent` runs catalog/status tests and a real Chrome/React fixture at
1200, 601, 600 and 393px, including delayed tab bars, the band/stack fallbacks, session navigation
and cleanup. It uses the existing desktop-profile Playwright installation and local Chrome; set `DSH
_MOBILE_PLAYWRIGHT` and `DSH_MOBILE_CHROME` to use other installations. It does not launch or change
a running DSH host.
## Unread conversations
When a run finishes while you are viewing another conversation, the sidebar marks that conversation
with a green dot. Opening it lands at the beginning of its latest answer instead of the bottom of th
e transcript, so the answer can be read from its first line. The landing waits for the host to resto
re the conversation, uses the same reading inset as the navigation controls, and backs off as soon a
s you scroll yourself. Its switch, **Unread conversation opens at the answer**, lives in **Settings
→ UI Beautify → Interface enhancements** and defaults on.
## Floating quick actions
A draggable button floats at the bottom-right of an open conversation. Its position is kept in the b
rowser, so it survives a reload, and the button rests just above the message box rather than over it
s send button; drag it anywhere inside the window. Clicking it opens a host menu with three shortcut
s for the conversation on screen:
- **Archive this conversation** — the host's own archive action; once archived it opens the next con
versation by the same priority instead of leaving you on a blank new-conversation page, and a conver

sation that is still running disables the row and says why.
- **Pin this conversation** / **Unpin th

is conversation** — follows the host's pinned state, the same one the sidebar's pin marker shows.
